Karthik / Laura — forwarding Remedy's reply. They're pressing for 30-day notice and a 30-day run-out with a capped fee.

My suggested negotiation position:
- Auto-renew notice: propose split-notice cadence — 60 days for material contract renewals, 45 days for standard Order Form renewals that do not include reserved capacity changes. This preserves our ability to plan capacity while giving them flexibility.
- Termination for convenience: counter with a 90-day run-out with option for a 45-day expedited run-out if Remedy pays a one-time transition fee equal to 25% of one month’s ARR (or prepaid support credits).
- Data/export: agree to standard 30-days for data export and provide an optional escrow addendum if Remedy requires it for an additional one-time fee.

Karthik — can you draft redline language for the split-notice approach and the two-tier run-out (90 days default / 45 days expedited paid option)? If that looks reasonable I'll propose it back to Maggie and include a DocuSign stub.

Thanks,
Irene
Attachment: proposed_split_notice_template.txt (text snippet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FW: Redlines: Term / Auto-renew / Termination-for-Convenience — proposed exit mechanics

Irene / Laura —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed Remedy's requests and drafted clause language below (redline-ready). High-level guidance: do not accept a flat 30-day opt-out — operationally risky. Split-notice is defensible and easier to explain to operations. Proposed language:  

"Notice of Non-Renewal. Except as set forth below, either party may elect not to renew an Order Form by providing written notice to the other party at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. For Routine Order Forms (defined as Order Forms that do not reserve dedicated capacity, do not include pre-committed GPU pools, and where annual spend is below $250,000), the parties agree that forty-five (45) days' prior written notice shall be sufficient to effect non-renewal."

"Termination for Convenience; Run-Out. Either party may terminate an Order Form for convenience upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may elect an expedited run-out of forty-five (45) days by paying a one-time transition fee equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the monthly recurring fees in effect as of the date of termination. During any run-out period Redwood will provide commercially reasonable assistance to allow orderly data export and handover."
If Remedy insists on a 30-day notice we should escalate to VP Legal; 30 days materially increases our risk.

I can produce a tracked-change Word doc if you want; otherwise happy for Laura to mirror this into the Order Form appendix.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: k_terminology_snippet.patch (inline clause text)

Hi Maggie — thanks for your patience while we reviewed internally. Per the thread below, Redwood can accept a compromise that should address Remedy's operational timelines while keeping our capacity planning intact. Proposed final language (included in attached redline):

- Split notice cadence: 45 days for Routine Order Forms; 60 days for Reserved/Capacity Order Forms.
- Termination run-out: 90 days default; customer may elect an expedited 45-day run-out with a one-time transition fee equal to 25% of the monthly recurring fees.
- Data export / escrow: Redwood will provide standard data export within 30 days post-termination. If Remedy requires formal escrow, we can add an escrow addendum at a one-time fee; please indicate if you want that in the DocuSign packet.

If the above is acceptable, I've prepared a DocuSign envelope here: https://app.docusign.com/some-doc-link/REM-7345. Please review the attached redline (Remedy_Redline_MSA_v3.docx) where we've tracked these updates.

Requested next steps:
1) Maggie / Remedy Legal to confirm whether escrow addendum is required (yes/no).
2) Remedy to confirm PO issuance timeline once DocuSign is signed.
3) Redwood to issue invoice for any agreed transition fee if Remedy elects expedited run-out.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the language; otherwise please sign the DocuSign and we'll route to procurement for PO issuance.

Best,
